word.partOfSpeech: preposition (always with the dative); separable prefix

pronunciation.notes: Au as in 'house'. It's the same word as English 'out'.

word.meaning: from (origin); out of; made of; over, off
word.shortDefinition: Where something comes from or goes out of.

intro.title: Woher kommst du?
paragraphs: Ich komme aus Brasilien: I come from Brazil. Aus tells where someone or something comes from, and out of what. Like mit, it always takes the dative.

etymology.title: Where it comes from
etymology.summary: Aus and English 'out' are the same word.

tables.title: aus + dative
notes: Countries without an article need nothing extra: aus Spanien. With an article: aus der Türkei, aus den USA.

wordFamily.english: to be off; to be over
to get off, to turn off

keyTrap.title: The big trap: von or aus?
keyTrap.explanation: For your home country or city, German uses aus. Von is for people and for starting points.

correct.german: Ich komme gerade von der Arbeit.
correct.literal: I come just from the work.
correct.note: Coming back from a place or activity: von.

commonMistakes.title: Made of
commonMistakes.explanation: Aus also says what something is made of.

examples.english: The table is made of wood.

sampleSentences.german: Sie trinkt Kaffee aus einer großen Tasse.
sampleSentences.english: She drinks coffee from a big cup.

sampleSentences.german: Die Schule ist um eins aus.

memoryHook: Aus = out. Out of a country (aus Spanien), out of a cup, out of wood. Always with the dative.

quiz.prompt: Woher kommst du? – Ich komme ___ Italien.
